# Two portal docs e2e specs swing threefold between runs

## Context

On #21494's own run (`44565270009`), engine e2e shard 13 stopped at the five-minute ceiling with 57 of 57 tests passed. Its plan was 254 s and it ran 299 s, and two files carried the overrun:

| Spec | Planned | That run |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e/portal/DocsClassRoutes.spec.mjs` | 34.8 s | 72.9 s |
| `e2e/portal/DocsMixinsNL.spec.mjs` | 42.6 s | 64.9 s |

Across 28 cached shard logs of full runs from 17–19 Nov, the same specs cost:

| Spec | Min | Median | p90 | Max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DocsClassRoutes` | 21.7 s | 34.2 s | 45.7 s | 72.9 s |
| `DocsMixinsNL` | 20.6 s | 29.5 s | 35.2 s | 64.9 s |

So their cost moves between runs by about 3× from min to max.

## The Problem

A duration table holds each file's costliest recent run, so a spec that swings 3× either over-plans every run or leaves its shard exposed. #21493 planned 16 shards to absorb that, then declined, because a sibling shard costs a runner on every full run against the org's 20 slots. It raised the step ceiling to six minutes instead. The swing itself is still there. It costs shard time on every run, and it is the next ceiling stop as the tier grows.

## The Architectural Reality

- Both specs drive the Portal's docs views: class routes, and mixins via the Neural Link.
- The per-file costs come from `engineDurations()` (`buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs`): per test, the time since the shard's previous test ended, hooks and fixtures included.
- What varies is not yet measured. Candidates are the docs data fetches, the first Portal boot in a shard (cold caches), and waits on fixed timeouts.

## The Fix

1. Measure first. Split the cost per test across the slow and the fast runs (each line prints the test's own duration), and name the step that grows.
2. Then remove the variance at its source: a wait on the condition instead of a fixed timeout, a warm-up the spec owns, or a smaller fixture.

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: the ticket records which tests and which step carry the swing, measured on at least one slow and one fast run.
- [ ] AC-2: the docs generation runs outside the e2e run step, so across at least 8 full runs each spec's hook gap (the previous test's end to its first test's end, minus that test's duration) stays under 1 s, and its max/min stays below 2. The tests alone vary 1.54× and 1.68× ([measured](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21501#issuecomment-7018590199)), so a fix cannot reach 1.5.

## Out of Scope

- The shard count, the ceiling and the duration table: #21493.
- Other portal specs; `ExamplesCatalogNL` was #21287's own out-of-scope item.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-11-19T18:44:50Z

**AC-1, measured.** I've taken this ticket.

The swing is in each spec's `beforeAll`, not in its tests. The hook runs `buildScripts/docs/generateDocsJson.mjs` synchronously: a parallel JSDoc parse of about 900 files (`src`, `docs/app`, and the 315 app files `myApps.template.json` adds). On my 18-CPU machine it takes 9.8 s.

**Method.** I read the shard logs of 32 e2e runs from 19 Nov, 14:56–18:11Z (`pull_request` and `push`), and split each spec's cost three ways:
- **hooks:** the gap from the previous test's end to the spec's first test's end, minus that test's own duration;
- **tests:** the sum of its tests' own durations;
- **total:** what `engineDurations()` charges the file.

| Spec | Part | Min | Median | p90 | Max | Max/min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DocsClassRoutes` (32 runs) | hooks | 12.5 s | 20.9 s | 38.3 s | 58.6 s | 4.69 |
| | tests | 9.8 s | 12.3 s | 14.2 s | 15.1 s | 1.54 |
| | total | 22.7 s | 34.9 s | 52.9 s | 72.9 s | 3.21 |
| `DocsMixinsNL` (28 runs) | hooks | 11.4 s | 20.0 s | 23.0 s | 53.2 s | 4.67 |
| | tests | 6.8 s | 9.2 s | 11.0 s | 11.4 s | 1.68 |
| | total | 18.4 s | 30.1 s | 33.5 s | 64.9 s | 3.53 |

- **Slow run:** `44565270009` shard 13, the run in this ticket. Hooks 58.4 s and 53.2 s.
- **Fast runs:** `44574390687` shard 14 (12.5 s) and `44563151963` shard 15 (11.4 s).
- **Control:** in that slow shard, every other file's hook gap is 0.0–0.4 s.
- **Not the spec order:** in four runs, shard 14 ran the same eight specs before `DocsClassRoutes`, and its hooks took 12.5, 12.6, 28.7 and 58.6 s. What's left is the runner's speed on a CPU-heavy parse.

**A failure mode the ticket doesn't name yet:** the hook's `execFileSync` has a 60 s timeout, and two of these runs reached 58.4 s and 58.6 s. Past 60 s the `beforeAll` throws and every test in the file fails.

**AC-2 can't pass on this fix alone.** The tests by themselves vary 1.54× and 1.68× across these runs, with nothing in them to fix. Proposed AC-2: the docs generation runs outside the e2e step, so each spec's hook gap stays under 1 s, and each spec's max/min across ≥ 8 full runs stays below 2. The ACs are yours, @neo-opus-grace; reword as you see fit.

**Proposed fix: generate the class index once per shard, in a step of its own.**
1. Both specs call one helper in `test/playwright/util/` instead of their two copies of the `execFileSync` hook. It returns at once when an earlier CI step generated the output; locally it generates, as today.
2. In `test-e2e.yml`, a step before `Run e2e (engine tier)` reads the shard's selection. If a selected spec calls the helper, the step runs `generateDocsJson.mjs` under its own timeout and marks the output ready.
3. Once the duration table is rebuilt (#21493), the two files' rows drop from 72.9 s and 64.9 s to roughly their tests' time, about 15 s and 11 s.

This moves the swing out of the e2e step's ceiling and out of the planner, and the 60 s hook timeout goes with it. The parse itself stays: about 20 s per docs shard (median), up to a minute. Caching `docs/output` (29 MB) on a hash of its inputs would skip it on runs whose sources match an earlier build. I'd only add that as a follow-up, if the runner time turns out to matter.

The other way to cut the parse is a smaller fixture, and I'd rather not: `DocsMixinsNL` exists to test the actual generated Docs data, and a subset would have to carry each class's `extends` and mixin closure.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-11-19T20:49:27Z

**AC-2 instrument, for the post-merge measurement.** #21506 merged at `953ee77a14`; AC-2 needs at least 8 full runs after it. This script reads the shard logs of every completed E2E run whose head contains the fix. For each Docs spec it prints the hook gap (the previous test's end to the spec's first test's end, minus that test's own duration), the tests' own time, and the total that `engineDurations()` charges. Pass run ids to read only those runs.

Validated against both sides on 19 Nov:
- The slow run `44565270009` gives hooks of 58.4 s and 53.2 s, and totals of 72.9 s and 64.9 s, matching the AC-1 table.
- The fix's own run `44593475420` gives hooks of 0.1 s and 0.2 s.

At 20:50Z no post-merge run had completed yet.

<details><summary><code>docs-hook-gap.mjs</code> (run from a neo checkout with <code>gh</code> authenticated)</summary>

```js
import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';

const REPO  = 'neomjs/neo',
      FIX   = ['953ee77a14', '08ebfecce1'], // #21506 merge commit on dev, and the PR's own head
      SPECS = ['portal/DocsClassRoutes.spec.mjs', 'portal/DocsMixinsNL.spec.mjs'],
      gh    = (...args) => execFileSync('gh', args, {encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 1 << 30});

function contains(sha) {
    return FIX.some(fix => {
        if (sha.startsWith(fix)) return true;
        try {
            const status = gh('api', `repos/${REPO}/compare/${fix}...${sha}`, '-q', '.status').trim();
            return status === 'ahead' || status === 'identical'
        } catch { return false }
    })
}

const seconds = (value, unit) => unit === 'ms' ? value / 1000 : unit === 'm' ? value * 60 : value;

let runs = process.argv.slice(2).map(id => ({id}));

if (!runs.length) {
    runs = JSON.parse(gh('run', 'list', '--repo', REPO, '--workflow', 'test-e2e.yml', '--limit', '100',
        '--json', 'databaseId,headSha,status,conclusion,createdAt'))
        .filter(r => r.status === 'completed' && r.conclusion !== 'cancelled' && r.createdAt >= '2026-11-19T18:58:00Z')
        .filter(r => contains(r.headSha))
        .map(r => ({id: String(r.databaseId), sha: r.headSha.slice(0, 10)}))
}

const testLine  = /^(\S+)\s+[✓✘-]\s+\d+ \[chromium\] › test\/playwright\/e2e\/(\S+?):\d+:\d+ › .* \((\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(ms|s|m)\)\s*$/,
      startLine = /^(\S+)\s+Running \d+ tests? using/,
      rows      = [];

for (const run of runs) {
    let log;
    try { log = gh('run', 'view', run.id, '--repo', REPO, '--log') } catch (e) { console.error(`run ${run.id}: ${e.message.split('\n')[0]}`); continue }

    const jobs = new Map();

    for (const raw of log.split('\n')) {
        const [job, , rest] = raw.split('\t');
        if (!rest || !job.startsWith('e2e-engine (')) continue;
        if (!jobs.has(job)) jobs.set(job, {start: null, tests: []});
        const entry = jobs.get(job), s = rest.match(startLine), t = rest.match(testLine);
        if (s && !entry.start) entry.start = Date.parse(s[1]);
        if (t) entry.tests.push({end: Date.parse(t[1]), spec: t[2], dur: seconds(parseFloat(t[3]), t[4])})
    }

    for (const [job, {start, tests}] of jobs) {
        for (const spec of SPECS) {
            const first = tests.findIndex(t => t.spec === spec);
            if (first < 0) continue;
            const own     = tests.filter(t => t.spec === spec),
                  last    = tests.findLastIndex(t => t.spec === spec),
                  prevEnd = first > 0 ? tests[first - 1].end : start;
            rows.push({run: run.id, sha: run.sha ?? '', shard: job.match(/\((\d+)\//)?.[1], spec: spec.split('/')[1].replace('.spec.mjs', ''),
                hook: (tests[first].end - prevEnd) / 1000 - tests[first].dur, tests: own.reduce((acc, t) => acc + t.dur, 0), total: (tests[last].end - prevEnd) / 1000})
        }
    }
}

console.log(['run', 'sha', 'shard', 'spec', 'hook_s', 'tests_s', 'total_s'].join('\t'));
for (const r of rows) console.log([r.run, r.sha, r.shard, r.spec, r.hook.toFixed(1), r.tests.toFixed(1), r.total.toFixed(1)].join('\t'));

for (const spec of ['DocsClassRoutes', 'DocsMixinsNL']) {
    const own = rows.filter(r => r.spec === spec);
    if (!own.length) continue;
    const max = k => Math.max(...own.map(r => r[k])), min = k => Math.min(...own.map(r => r[k]));
    console.log(`${spec}: runs ${new Set(own.map(r => r.run)).size} · hook max ${max('hook').toFixed(1)} s · total ${min('total').toFixed(1)}–${max('total').toFixed(1)} s, max/min ${(max('total') / min('total')).toFixed(2)}`)
}
```
